## Body

F214 audit BEFORE: pij's warm/cold verdict at delivery vs what the seat's next model call did

WINDOW: 2026-11-12T03:36Z to 2026-11-19T03:36Z (7 days; epoch ms 1794454565250 to 1795059365250), the whole live fleet (every folder under /Users/jordanknight), live store ~/.pij-rs/pij.sqlite read-only.

COMMANDS (receipts; the audit is read-only and launches nothing in the daemon):
  1. pij-rs fleet-report /Users/jordanknight --since 7d --threads 2 --out /tmp/f214/fr-all
     -> 107188 calls, 16757 turns, 755 sessions (used for its sessions->seat map and the claude-code/OMP calls with their native cw_5m/cw_1h split; read-only, fleet_report not edited)
  2. python3 /tmp/f214/audit.py ~/.pij-rs/pij.sqlite /tmp/f214/fr-all 1794454565250 1795059365250 --json /tmp/f214/audit-before.json
     Copilot calls are read straight from ~/.copilot/session-state/<sid>/events.jsonl session.usage_record (conversation-agent only; subagent and utility calls excluded), because fleet_report's cache_ttl_s for Copilot is an assumed 3600, not the record's.

METHOD:
- Spine: every delivery.outcome = delivered in the window (14620), deduped per seat to the first delivery before each next main-chain call; paired with the seat's previous call (idle, context) and its next call within 15 min (13404 paired).
- pij's verdict at send time (message.pushed `at` when the msg id matches, else the delivery `at`), reconstructed with today's rules: daemon state from the last seat.activity; guard = busy if working, cold if ctx > 400k and idle > 60 min (COLD_IDLE_MS), else clear; the CACHE column = idle vs the TTL pij gets today (Claude/OMP: 1h if the last call wrote 1h, 5m if it wrote 5m; Copilot: only 300 s and 3600 s map, anything else (1800) is unknown).
- Truth: the next call's cacheRead share of its total prompt. Warm >= 50%, cold < 10%, partial between (660, excluded). Busy deliveries (3370) excluded from the rates. Decided: 9402.
- "Silent cold wake" = pij treated the seat as warm (idle <= 60 min, no refusal, no warning) and the next call re-wrote the cache. "False cold" = pij treated it cold, the call read the cache.

FINDINGS (what this means for the fix shape):
1. The dominant error is NOT the unknown GPT TTL. It is the guard ignoring a TTL pij already knows. 727 of the 785 silent cold wakes (and 257 of the 265 large ones) are on seats whose TTL pij has as 5 min (Copilot plain Claude, cacheTtlSeconds 300: 583; OMP via github-copilot, 5m writes: 144). pij's CACHE column already calls them cold; cold_wake::check uses only the fixed 60-min COLD_IDLE_MS, so they go through with no word. Median idle 12 min (Copilot) and 19 min (OMP). The large ones re-wrote ~101M (Copilot plain) and ~25M (OMP) context tokens in the week.
2. GPT (cachePolicyTtlSeconds 1800): pij has the TTL as unknown on every delivery (180 sol + 45 astra + 28 sol-5.6). 21% of those sol deliveries were actually cold; 19 were silent cold wakes (3 large). Mapping "30m" into a real duration fixes this class outright.
3. OMP GPT records no cache writes, so no TTL at all (173 unknown; only 4 cold, and 13 false-cold under the 60-min rule: GPT's cache outlived 60 min there). This is where the config/table rungs (models.yml cacheRetention, then a table) are needed.
4. Native evidence is good but not perfect: Copilot cacheExpiresAt called 285 large plain-Claude deliveries cold, 36 of which (12.6%) still read the cache (Anthropic's TTL is a minimum; mostly 5-6 min idles), and called 2 warm that were cold. For a brake that is the safe direction.
5. Claude Code direct (1h, split-derived) is already right: 0.2-0.4% errors, all false-cold.
6. Busy deliveries are 25% of all pairings and never misclassified-cold (the busy rule is sound).

DECISION NEEDED (I proceed on my recommendation unless you say otherwise; only the guard wiring depends on it):
Making the send-time cold check use the real TTL (packet item 3) turns ~285 of 983 large non-busy deliveries to Copilot-plain Claude seats per week (29%), and 75 of 326 to OMP github-copilot Claude, from silently-allowed into refusals (E-RS-COLD-WAKE, needs --force/--fyi). Today only 40 and 7 are refused. That is the correct brake by the numbers, but it is a large behaviour change for 5-min-TTL seats.
  (a) RECOMMENDED: guard refuses on lifetime = the seat's real TTL (evidence order native > proxy > config > table, basis shown) for large seats; COLD_IDLE_MS stays only as the ceiling. Unknown TTL + large + idle beyond the shortest table TTL for its route warns (never refuses).
  (b) Keep refusal at 60 min; between TTL and 60 min WARN only (receipt + sender-visible line), refuse past 60 min. Smaller behaviour change, still ends the silence.
I am building (a)'s data model (CacheTtl -> real duration with basis, cacheExpiresAt carried through, size/status columns, warm flush, idle nudge) now; the guard threshold is one line either way.

AFTER-AUDIT PLAN: same two commands after deploy, window starting at the deploy time, plus a 'post-fix verdict' column computed by the shipped rule; compare silent-cold and false-cold per row above.
